description: capafy-loop-cli.sh and life-manager-loop-cli.sh both build STARTUP as a fully single-quoted bash string (`STARTUP='...'`). Inside single quotes, backslash has no special meaning -- it is a literal character. Both files contain exactly one `\$` sequence each (grep-confirmed) intended to produce a literal dollar sign in the prompt text (e.g. 'revenue is \$0'), but since single quotes never expand `$` in the first place, the backslash was unnecessary and is NOT consumed -- the literal two-character sequence backslash-dollar is what actually gets sent to the spawned claude process ('revenue is \$0' rather than 'revenue is $0'). Not a shell syntax error and unlikely to derail the LLM's understanding, but it is a real escaping mistake left in place by this fix pass and pollutes the exact prompt text with a stray backslash.

evidence.snippet: revenue is \$0 and the wall is our listings are not competitive/discoverable
